page: Amazon Web Services m7gd.16xlarge is a general-purpose, 7th-generation instance driven by the AWS Nitro System and custom AWS Graviton3-era hardware. It features 64 physical cores across 64 dedicated vCPUs built on the arm64 ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 architecture, running at a base clock of 2.6 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is balanced at 256.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per core). For high-throughput local operations, the server integrates 3,800 GB of NVMe SSD instance storage. It includes no discrete GPUs and operates with a 30 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark outcomes show distinct multi-core scaling alongside robust memory performance. In multi-threaded execution, the instance attains top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core (20,645.0) and Clang software compilation (58,683.0), supported by strong stress-ng multi-core throughput (97,895.22). Memory subsystems perform at high bandwidth levels, registering 253.41 GB/sec on large read blocks and earning a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3,142.14. Single-core measurements—such as Geekbench single-core (1,529.0) and stress-ng single-core (1,532.29)—fall within the average tier, indicating that aggregate compute scale rather than peak single-thread frequency defines its processing capacity.

The inclusion of 3,800 GB of fast NVMe SSD storage paired with 30 Gbps network connectivity creates high data efficiency for I/O-intensive workloads. In caching and data tier testing, it demonstrated strong throughput across Redis SET operations (102.0 million ops/sec), PassMark database operations (31,226.41), and static web serving (73.92 GB/sec). Large language model prompt evaluation is similarly competitive, processing 2,675.92 tokens/sec on lightweight models, though text generation speed is comparatively modest on smaller architectures.

The hardware tradeoffs center on its arm64 instruction set and lack of x86 vector extensions (such as AVX-512) or hardware accelerators. Software ecosystems must support ARM architecture natively to realize optimal execution efficiency. With its combination of balanced RAM, 64 physical cores, and large bundled NVMe storage, the m7gd.16xlarge is suitable for container clusters, intermediate database deployments, large software build pipelines, distributed caching layers, and high-concurrency web serving.
